{{Short description|American statistician}}
[[File:Sally C Morton portrait.jpg|thumb|180px|Sally C. Morton]]
'''Sally C. Morton''' is an American [[statistics|statistician]] specializing in [[comparative effectiveness research]]. In 2021, Morton joined [[Arizona State University]] as executive vice president of Knowledge Enterprise, the administrative subdivision of Arizona State involving university research.{{r|ktar}} Morton is also a professor in the College of Health Solutions and the School of Mathematical Statistical Sciences and holds the Florence Ely Nelson Chair at Arizona State.

Morton was educated at [[Stanford University]] and the [[London School of Economics]]. Her PhD thesis, ''Interpretable Projection Pursuit'', was completed at Stanford in 1990, under the tutelage of [[Jerome H. Friedman]].{{r|MathGenealogy}} Before joining ASU, Morton was dean of the College of Science and professor of statistics at [[Virginia Tech]]. Prior to this role, she worked at [[RTI International]], the [[RAND Corporation]] and the [[University of Pittsburgh]].{{r|newdean|chair}}

Morton was 2009 president of the [[American Statistical Association]] (ASA) and 2013 chair of Section U (Statistics) of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] (AAAS).{{r|norwood}} She is a fellow of the ASA and of the AAAS, and an elected member of the Society for Research Synthesis Methodology and the [[International Statistical Institute]] (ISI).{{r|newdean|chair}} She won the [[American Statistical Association Founders Award]] in 2015{{r|founder}} and is the 2017 winner of the Janet L. Norwood Award.{{r|norwood}} She was elected to the [[National Academy of Medicine]] in 2024.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://nam.edu/member/?member_id=UPVa4wPGkbhRgvp5eP81Kw%3D%3D|title= Dr. Sally C Morton, Ph.D. |work= National Academy of Medicine |accessdate=November 12, 2024}}</ref>
